problem: Earlier VLN surveys (Gu et al. 2022, Park & Kim 2023, Wu et al. 2024) predate foundation models and give bottom-up summaries of benchmarks and conventional (LSTM-era) methods. None covers how pre-trained models, LLMs and VLMs are used to tackle VLN challenges, and none links VLN problems to a general reasoning and planning framework that foundation-model researchers would recognise.
motivation: Foundation models such as BERT/LXMERT-style pre-trained transformers, CLIP, GPT-4 and VLMs have changed VLN research. The focus has moved from multimodal attention and policy learning toward large-scale pre-training, LLM-based planning, commonsense reasoning and zero-shot agents. The authors see VLN's core difficulties (representing and generalising environments, interpreting ambiguous human language, grounded reasoning and planning) as mapping naturally onto the LAW framework (Hu & Shu 2023), in which foundation models act as the world model and the agent model. They use this framework to organise the field top-down.
key_idea: Organise VLN challenges and foundation-model-era solutions top-down with the LAW framework, split into three parts: a world model (history/memory, cross-environment generalisation), a human model (ambiguous instructions, grounded-instruction generalisation) and a VLN agent (grounding/reasoning, planning, foundation models as agents), then derive future directions from each part.
insight: Several conclusions stand out. (1) History encoding moved from recurrent state tokens (RecBERT's [CLS], MTVM's memory bank) to full-sequence hierarchical encoders (HAMT). Only the latter allow efficient large-scale pre-training on instruction–path pairs, and they later branched into graph- and map-based memories (DUET, GridMM, BEVBert) and text-form maps for LLM agents (MapGPT, MC-GPT). (2) Pre-training on large in-domain augmented data (Prevalent, HM3D-AutoVLN, ScaleVLN, PanoGen, Marky/Kamath) has become the main driver of closing the human–agent gap. The survey states that in-domain pre-trained multimodal transformers outperform ones initialised from generic VLMs (Oscar, LXMERT). (3) LLMs are best seen as supplementary structured planners and commonsense sources, not full replacements. The authors argue that VLN's constrained action space makes coarse step-by-step LLM guidance useful, but LLM agents suffer from missing embodied experience, information loss when vision is captioned into text, and hallucination. The paper contains no ablations or experiments.
method: Benchmark taxonomy (Table 1): about 24 VLN benchmarks (R2R, R4R, RxR, SOON, REVERIE, CVDN, HANNA, VLN-CE, Robo-VLN, ALFRED, TEACh, DialFRED, Touchdown, AerialVLN, CARLA-based driving sets, etc.) classified along World (domain, environment), Human (turns, communication format, action- vs goal-directed granularity), Agent (robot/driving/aerial type, graph/discrete/continuous action space, extra manipulation/detection) and Dataset (human vs templated text, human vs planner routes).

World model section: history encoding (recurrent state tokens → HAMT hierarchical panorama+history transformers → text-described history for LLM agents), graph/map-based history (topological graphs, grid/semantic/BEV maps, linguistic maps in MapGPT/MC-GPT), and environment generalisation (CLIP/video visual features, EnvEdit/EnvMix/KED/FDA/Pathdreamer/SE3DS augmentation, pre-training on augmented environments).

Human model section: resolving ambiguous instructions with perceptual context and commonsense (VLN-Trans, LANA+, KERM, NavHint, LLM landmark co-occurrence, SayCan) and with information seeking (when/what to ask, LLMs as askers via conformal prediction or ICL, LLM/VLM oracles such as R2H and VLN-Copilot); grounded-instruction generalisation via pre-trained text representations (PRESS, VLN-BERT, PREVALENT, Airbert, ProbES, NavGPT-2) and instruction synthesis (Speaker-Follower, Marky, PASTS, SAS, SRDF, LANA).

VLN agent section: grounding and reasoning (explicit semantic grounding; VLN-specific pre-training tasks such as HOP, LOViS, masked path modeling, entity-aware pre-training), planning (graph-based planners such as DUET, ETPNav, BEVBert, GridMM, waypoint predictors, DreamWalker/lookahead; LLM planners such as LLM-Planner, A²Nav, VL-Map, SayNav), and foundation models as agents (single-stream VLM agents, CE transfer via waypoint predictors, zero-shot LLM agents such as NavGPT, MapGPT, DiscussNav, MC-GPT, InstructNav, and fine-tuned LLM/VLM agents such as NaviLLM, NaVid, LangNav, NavCoT).

Future directions: unified and realistic benchmarks (OVMM, BEHAVIOR-1K), dynamic environments (HAZARD, Habitat 3.0, HA-VLN), indoor→outdoor/driving/aerial; 2D→3D world representations (CLIP-feature 3D maps, scene graphs, 3D foundation models); instruction→free-form dialogue; LLM limitations (lack of embodied experience, hallucination, planning weaknesses); sim-to-real deployment (perception and embodiment gaps, teleoperation data).

setting.observation: n/a (survey covers panoramic RGB(-D), egocentric RGB, etc.)
setting.action_space: n/a (survey covers nav-graph, discrete low-level, and continuous action spaces)
setting.simulator: n/a (surveys Matterport3D simulator, Habitat, AI2-THOR, CARLA, AirSim, Google Street View, real world)

numbers_note: Survey paper: no experiments and no quantitative results tables. The only table is a qualitative benchmark taxonomy (Table 1).
results: No empirical results; this is a survey. Its main contribution is the LAW-based taxonomy (world model / human model / VLN agent) of foundation-model-era VLN methods, the benchmark taxonomy table covering about 24 datasets, and future directions: realistic and dynamic benchmarks, 3D world models, dialogue-based human models, embodied foundation models, hallucination mitigation and sim-to-real.
limitations: Qualitative only: no quantitative comparison or leaderboard of methods across R2R/REVERIE/R2R-CE etc., so it cannot be used for cross-paper numbers.

Coverage of LLM/VLM agents stops around mid/late-2024 and is fairly brief (e.g., little detail on fine-tuned video-VLM navigators or continuous-environment LLM agents); ObjectNav and other non-language navigation tasks are largely out of scope.
Framework categorisation is sometimes loose: some methods appear under several headings, and claims such as 'in-domain pre-training beats VLM initialisation' are stated without supporting tables.
builds_on: LAW framework (Hu & Shu 2023, language models, agent models, and world models)
